metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Slovenia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Slovenia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The document indicates that PISA was implemented across 81 countries and economies and that some countries/economies marked with an asterisk (*) did not meet all sampling standards, implying that OECD’s standard complex survey procedures were used in producing the reported estimates. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied, so the weighting implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. Analysts should rely on the PISA 2022 technical documentation and Reader’s Guide/annexes for the exact weighting and variance estimation approach used to compute the reported means, differences, confidence intervals, and correlations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarising descriptive PISA 2022 results (means, proficiency shares, relative success, and correlations) rather than an empirical student-level modelling study that reports a PV-based dependent variable. As a result, plausible values handling for achievement scores is not applicable in the sense required for ML/predictive extraction, and the factsheet does not report any missing-data handling procedure. The absence of PV/missing-data methodology is therefore due to the report’s purpose (summary of already-produced PISA estimates) rather than a transparency gap in an ML analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Slovenia analytic sample as 6,721 students in 345 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 18,900 15-year-olds in Slovenia. It does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA implementation and the note that some countries/economies with an asterisk (*) required caution due to not meeting one or more sampling standards; no further Slovenia-specific filtering rules are provided in the excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarises Slovenia’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas—across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Slovenia’s mean creative thinking score is 30/60, significantly below the OECD average (33). About 73% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), while 16% are top performers at Levels 5–6 (OECD average: 27%). Relative to mathematics and reading performance, creative thinking is below expectations, and 17% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely attributed to mathematics performance; the reported correlations are 0.6 (creative thinking–math) and 0.59 (creative thinking–reading). The factsheet provides descriptive and correlational benchmarks rather than an ML modelling pipeline, so no predictive-model performance metrics are reported here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (a descriptive reporting product) rather than an empirical ML/predictive research article. Consequently, fields required for ML extraction (e.g., PV handling choices for a model, missing-data handling strategy for an analysis, and ML algorithms with performance metrics) are not applicable or not reported in the provided text. The document focuses on already-estimated PISA indicators (means, proficiency levels, relative success differences, and correlations) and points readers to the main report/annexes for technical details.
